title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli multiplicities M_{g,ν}. He treats the Deligne–Mumford boundary as a normal crossings divisor Θ on a smooth 'multiplicité' (orbifold or stack) Y, with open part Y* = Y∖Θ. For a locally closed stratum, or more generally an immersion D'→Y into the boundary, he considers the deleted tubular neighbourhood V*_{D',Y}, i.e. the germ of Y* near D'. He wants its fundamental groupoid Π1 V*_{D',Y}.

The previous page defines specialization maps Π1 V*_{D'',Y} → Π1 V*_{D',Y} for a chain D''→D'→Y. To avoid choices of base points or domains, he uses a 'localized' fundamental groupoid built from subdomains and the isomorphisms between them.

This page has three parts.
(i) A general topos-theoretic setting: Y is a (simplicial) topos, and Y* is an open subtopos given by a subobject of the final object. D'→Y is required to factor through the closed complement Y∖Y*.
(ii) A transitivity property, which involves triple composites D'''→D''→D'→Y (238).
(iii) The plan: the normal crossings hypothesis will let him make Π1 V*_{D',Y} (and the D'' analogue) explicit in simpler terms, through equivalences with Π1 P_{D'*} and Π1 P_{D''*}. Here P_{D'*} is the punctured normal bundle of D' over the open stratum. For codimension d this is a bundle with fibre (C^*)^d, essentially a principal (C^*)^d- or (S^1)^d-bundle.

The theorem is begun at the bottom and finished on the next page (239). Take Y a multiplicity, Θ a normal crossings divisor, and D'→Y an immersion of codimension d factoring through Θ^(d). Then there is an equivalence of groupoids Π1 P_{D'*} → Π1 V*_{D',Y}, canonical up to unique isomorphism, compatible with composites. This is the groupoid version of 'tangential base points at infinity'. It is the mechanism that glues the fundamental groupoids of the boundary strata of M_{g,ν} into the Teichmüller tower and its structure at infinity. The left margin restates the task: make the needed properties of V_{D',Y} explicit in terms of the complex structure of D'→Y.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. There are two small gaps.

Gap 1: the general topos setting (Y a simplicial topos, Y* open) is only gestured at. A deleted 'tubular neighbourhood' of a closed subtopos, and its Π1, are not defined there. The normal-crossings comparison makes sense only in the analytic or topological case.
Gap 2: the phrase 'comme conséquences équivalentes à' is grammatically and logically unclear. Most likely the intended reading is 'as consequences of equivalences with Π1 P'.
The pair 'Π1 V*_{D',Y'}, Π1 V*_{D',Y}' looks like a slip. By parallelism with P_{D'*}, P_{D''*} it should probably read V*_{D'',Y} and V*_{D',Y} (in some order).

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum of a normal crossings divisor; its fundamental groupoid is equivalent to that of the punctured normal bundle ((C^*)^d-bundle) over the stratum, canonically up to unique isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of normal crossings complements; tangential base points / specialization to the normal cone; boundary ('at infinity') fundamental groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical topology (tubular neighbourhood theorem). In the algebraic/Galois setting: Grothendieck–Murre (tame π1), Deligne 1989 (tangential base points), Ihara–Nakamura and Nakamura (π1 near the boundary of M_{g,n})
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and 'structure à l'infini' only qualitatively, without this lemma

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoids defined through subdomains and the isomorphisms between them (localization), to get specialization maps without choosing base points, with transitivity for chains D'''→D''→D'→Y
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with many base points / stack-valued (sheaf of) fundamental groupoids; compatibility of specialization along flags of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (groupoid viewpoint in SGA1 and the Esquisse); compatibility along strata developed in Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (groupoid formalism); Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller groupoid)

ideas.what: Formulating the deleted-neighbourhood setup for a general (simplicial) topos with an open subtopos defined by a subobject of the final object
ideas.modern_name: Open/closed subtopos decomposition; vanishing-cycles style 'nearby' topos (cf. Deligne's oriented products / Gabber's oriented topos)
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA4 (open/closed subtopoi); Deligne, Laumon, Gabber (oriented products)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV (open and closed subtopoi)

missed.claim: Grothendieck intends to treat deleted neighbourhoods and their Π1 for a closed subtopos of an arbitrary (simplicial) topos, beyond analytic spaces. This would be a topos-intrinsic 'tubular neighbourhood at infinity'. He leaves it as a parenthetical and immediately specializes to the analytic normal-crossings case.
missed.quote: (des topos simpliciaux, disons ouverts ...) et un ouvert Y* de Y [plus gén.t un objet du topos Y ...]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates later notions such as oriented-product or nearby-cycle topoi and exit-path/stratified homotopy theory. It is not developed here, so it is at most a minor historical pointer.

deep.surprise_reason: The core statement is standard: the deleted neighbourhood of a normal-crossings stratum is equivalent, for Π1, to the punctured normal bundle, canonically. It is the groupoid form of tangential base points, later made explicit by Deligne, Ihara–Nakamura and others. The care about canonicity and the topos-level generality are pleasant details of Grothendieck's approach, but they are neither new results nor absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'comme conséquences équivalentes[?] à' should probably read 'comme conséquences d'équivalences à' (or 'avec').
'Π1 V*_{D',Y'}' is likely a slip for 'Π1 V*_{D'',Y}'; the first subscript in the image seems to carry a prime on Y, which is probably erroneous.
'Soient Y un espace multiplicité[?]' is most likely 'Soient Y une multiplicité analytique' or 'un espace (multiplicité)'. Grothendieck's term for an orbifold/stack is 'multiplicité'.
Left margin reads roughly: 'qualités à expliciter sur V_{D',Y} ... en termes de D'→Y complexe ... [?] W normaux à Y'. This is a partial reading.
'fait intervenir parfois[?]' may be 'fait intervenir aussi'.
